marker: # unit_length, patterns and ref_repeats are Table 1, which gives the consensus repeat unit, its
# length and the number of units in each of the three sequenced genomes. ref_size is the amplicon
# size Table 5 predicts for Z2491, the genome this scheme is anchored on.
# The two tables check each other exactly. At every locus the amplicon size minus the unit length
# times the repeat number is the same flanking length in all three genomes, Z2491, MC58 and FAM18,
# so the repeat numbers and the sizes confirm one another and nothing here is derived. In silico
# PCR reproduces all twelve Z2491 sizes, and running the same primers against MC58 reproduces all
# twelve of that genome's sizes as well, which checks the primers independently of the reference.
# patterns are kept at the nine loci where counting the published motif in Z2491 returns the
# published repeat number, so the tandem array cross-check is active there. They are left out at
# the two where it does not, which would otherwise flag COUNT_DISAGREES on every sample:
#   NMTR1  the counter returns 27 against the published 25; the 7 bp unit CAAACAA is A rich and
#          the array runs on into similar flanking sequence, while Table 1 places the array at
#          exactly 25 units, its span of 175 bp being 25 times 7.
#   NMTR6  the counter returns 1 against the published 2, the second copy of the 21 bp unit being
#          too diverged to match.
# NMTR12 IS A COMPOUND LOCUS and is reported by length only, as STTR3 is in STm_ECDC. Its array
# mixes a 13 bp unit, GGGCTGTAGAGAT, with a 12 bp unit, GGCTGTAGAGAT, in varying numbers, and the
# paper counts them together and writes the Z2491 allele as 3 = 2a1b. The single unit formula
# cannot express that, so unit_length is 0 and no repeat number is recorded; the amplicon is still
# sized and the allele has to be assigned by hand. The flanking length of 180 bp holds for this
# locus in all three genomes, so a total count can be recovered from a size once the mixture of
# the two units is known.
